chunks: Abu Qasim Abdullah ibn Ahmad told me, saying: Ali ibn Abdul Aziz told us, saying: Abu Na'eem told us, saying: Abdul Wahid ibn Aymain told us, saying: My father told me, from Ayesha,

that a man entered upon her asking her about the two units of prayer after the afternoon prayer. She said: 'By the One who took His soul (meaning the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family), he did not leave them until he met Allah, the Exalted, and until he became heavy (ill) from prayer, and he used to pray much of his prayer while sitting. I said: 'Indeed, when Umar took power, he forbade them.' She said: 'You are truthful, but the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not pray them in the mosque for fear that it would be a burden on his nation, and he loved what was easy for them.'

key_terms.ثَقُلَ عَنِ الصَّلَاةِ: became heavy from prayer (illness preventing standing)
key_terms.مَخَافَةَ أَنْ يُثْقِلَ: for fear of placing a burden

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad perform two units of prayer after Asr and why did Umar forbid it?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Aisha to highlight the Prophet’s consistent practice of the two Rak'ahs after Asr, emphasizing that he maintained this Sunnah even during his final illness. The text clarifies that Umar’s prohibition was not of the act itself but of making it a communal obligation in the mosque, as the Prophet preferred to keep it voluntary to avoid burdening the Ummah. This distinction underscores the Shia scholarly appreciation for the Prophet’s wisdom in balancing spiritual discipline with communal ease.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-106 Abul Qasim Abdullah ibn Ahmad narrated that Ali ibn Abdul Aziz quoted Abu Na’eem, on the authority of Abdul Vahid ibn Aymain, on the authority of his father, “I went to see Ayesha and asked her about the two units of prayers after the afternoon prayers.

She said, ‘I swear by God who will take away his soul (i.e. the Prophet’s soul), the Prophet (MGB) never stopped saying those two units of prayers until he (MGB) went to meet the Honorable the Exalted God (perished), except for when he (MGB) was ill and could not say the prayers in a standing position. He said most of his prayers in a standing position.’ I asked her, ‘However, when Umar was in power, he admonished against these prayers.’ She said, ‘You are right. However, God’s Prophet (MGB) never said these prayers in the mosque, since he (MGB) feared that this might place a burden on his nation. Thus, he preferred to hide this from them.’”
